q-24393.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14217628/assets/f57f1223c28fc554909be6bbd2e8eafefa21a886b1a5abb47549f17bfa12e2ab.png)

For the parabola shown above, find the vertex and the equation of the axis of symmetry.
q-24393.worked_solution:
The vertex is the "turning point" of the parabola. In an upwards parabola, like the one here, the vertex is the minimum point. So, the vertex of this parabola is $(3,-2).$

The axis of symmetry is the vertical line that passes through the vertex. Therefore, the axis of symmetry of this parabola is $x=3.$

The equation of the curve above is $y=-{x}^{2}+2x+k.$ Find the value of $k.$
q-106046.worked_solution:
Notice that if we substitute $x=0$ into the given equation, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-{x}^{2}-x+k \\ y & =-(0)^{2}+2(0)+k \\ y & =k,\end{aligned}
$$

meaning that the curve intercepts the $y$-axis at the point $(0,k).$ Based on the graph, we see that we must have $k=5$ since our parabola intercepts the $y$-axis at $(0,5).$
